references.text: The beginning of Abraham's negotiation with God, where he starts by asking if fifty righteous people can spare Sodom, provides the immediate context for verse 28.
God remembered Abraham and sent Lot out of destruction—the direct result of Abraham's intercession for Sodom.
The psalm highlights God's mercy, grace, and patience, which is reflected in his willingness to spare Sodom for an ever-decreasing number of righteous people.
God says that if they find one righteous person in Jerusalem, he will forgive the city—a strong thematic parallel to Abraham's negotiation over how many righteous are needed to spare Sodom.
Without a remnant of righteous people, Jerusalem would have become like Sodom and Gomorrah—thematically linked to the idea that a few righteous can save an entire city.
God seeks a man who can stand in the gap and intercede—a parallel to Abraham's role as an intercessor for Sodom.
